title: A follow-up that asks a question doesn't wake the ticket's autopilot
description:
## Why

A follow-up sent to a finished session (`POST /dispatch` with `followUpTo`) inherits that session's ticket, and its finishing wakes the ticket's autopilot lineage. That's right when the follow-up is more work on the ticket. It's wrong when the follow-up is only a question: for example, asking a builder after the ticket is Done what made the work hard. Each such question restarts an autopilot that has nothing to do, which costs a run and adds noise to the ticket.

## What we want

A way to send a follow-up that doesn't wake anything when it finishes. Its answer still lands where it would today. Follow-ups that are real work keep waking the lineage as they do now.

## Research findings

Pruned at close-out: the cause (a follow-up's finish walks `followUpTo` to the root edge in `addFeedback` and wakes the autopilot) and the chosen mechanism (`subscription: "none"`, follow-up only) are implemented as described below. Full text is preserved in the task snapshots (latest pre-prune capture 2026-11-03T18:25:03Z) and the comment trail.

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2258](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2258>) (merged as `7797c306`), with the plan-review notes applied (kickoff clears a stray `followUpTo`; null/undefined presence test; plain docs wording; `docs/proxy-integration.md` and `docs/dispatch-protocol.md` updated; store witness checks the edge doc). No deviations from the plan's design. Close-out added the recommend-lane refusal test and one doc-line correction (commit `64e922fe`). The full plan, decisions and witnesses are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

Outside follow-up: LIN-4174 (a "question only" control on the run-page reply box and Flight Companion).

fits one session
plan-review due: no

comments.body:
## Research notes: LIN-4166 (grounded at LinearViewer `048c3319`; origin/main `ff1f4aa5` touches none of these files)

### Re-ground
Ticket references: `POST /dispatch` + `followUpTo`, the "inherits the ticket" behaviour, and the lineage wake. Running `git log --since=2026-11-03T17:14:24Z` over `lib/dispatch-store.js`, `lib/dispatch-wake.js`, `lib/dispatch-fields.js`, `lib/dispatch-entrance.js`, `lib/dispatch-factory.js`, `lib/dispatch-validation.js`, `lib/proxy-instructions.js`, `routes/proxy-dispatch.js` and `routes/dispatch.js` returns nothing on HEAD or on origin/main, so the ticket's description still holds.

### How the wake actually happens (confirmed by a spike)
1. A follow-up row stores `followUpTo` and inherits the anchor's issue, `sessionGroupId` and `rootItemId` (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:704-721`, `inheritFromAnchor`). It does **not** get a `sessionId`.
2. When feedback lands on the follow-up row, `addFeedback` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:3264-3330`) finds a wake event and calls `_resolveEdgeDoc` (`:2971-2983`). That walks the `followUpTo` chain to the **root** dispatch, which carries the up-chain edge (`sessionId` = the autopilot, plus `subscription`).
3. `buildWakeFollowUp(edgeDoc, …)` (`lib/dispatch-wake.js:166-229`) has deliberately **no** `followUpTo` guard (LIN-843: stepper beats must wake). Terminals and `[blocked]` always bubble, whatever the edge's `subscription`. The result is a `kind:'wake'` row with `followUpTo: <autopilot id>` and `queueIfBusy: true`, which resumes the finished autopilot.
4. The only existing suppressors are the `kind:'wake'` loop guard, self-edge, `abort` rows, the per-item `terminalWakeItems` once-guard, and LIN-4080's `_wakeParentStopped` (`:501-508`, recorded stop or halt `stop` only). A Done ticket's autopilot is *finished*, not *stopped*, so none of these fire.
5. The fan-out is worse than one run. If the woken autopilot is a child autopilot, its terminal on the wake row walks to *its* root and wakes the coordinator too (LIN-1059 path).

Spike (scratchpad `node:test` against `DispatchQueueStore` + mock collections): autopilot → worker `[done]` (1 wake), then a follow-up `{followUpTo: worker}` posts `[done] answered`, giving **2 wakes to the autopilot**, both reading "A child session reached a terminal outcome — resume your cross-check." This reproduces the ticket.

### Per-layer audit
- **Wake seam (`lib/dispatch-store.js` addFeedback, `:3264-3330`).** This is the single place a follow-up's finish turns into a wake. The two wake row producers are `_mintWake` (terminal/blocked) and the unguarded `[pending]` `addItem`. Both read the same `wakeFollowUp` local, and the `addItem` census (`tests/unit/lin-4080-addItem-census.test.js:25-34`) pins the whole set to 4 callers. A gate here covers every wake class. `nullWakeReason` is logged at `:3490`, so a suppressed wake attributes itself in the log. The gate must run **before** `_resolveEdgeDoc`, the grant lookup, provisioning and the `terminalWakeItems` CAS. Otherwise a suppressed wake could burn the witness or a credential (the same burn-before-decide rule LIN-4080 followed).
- **Wake matrix (`lib/dispatch-wake.js`).** `SUBSCRIPTION_LEVELS = ['everything','terminal-only']` (`:56`) is the single source of truth, imported by every validator. `buildWakeFollowUp` reads only the *edge's* `subscription`. Doctrine (`:13-21`, LIN-900 §5): terminals always bubble on an edge, so an edge can't be silenced. That's correct for orchestrator edges and must stay.
- **Run-field registry (`lib/dispatch-fields.js:150-162, 186-211`).** `subscription` is already a stored, every-hop run field (`src.subscription || 'terminal-only'`), threaded through `addItem`, the archive hop and both formatters. The spike confirmed `doc.subscription` survives queue → take → history. **No new plumbing is needed.**
- **Entrance lanes (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:225, 288-296, 401-406`).** `subscription` is validated by one step in the session lane (`POST /api/dispatch`, the run-page reply box), the proxy lane (`POST /api/proxy/dispatch`), the recommend lane and the kickoff lane. The step currently sees only `{subscription}`. The kickoff lane has no `followUpTo`, so a "requires followUpTo" rule written into this step would refuse a kickoff `'none'` automatically. The cross-field style already exists ("force requires followUpTo, abort, or an issueIdentifier", `lib/dispatch-validation.js:284`; "cascade requires abort", `:136`).
- **Factory inheritance (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:704-721`).** "Inherits the ticket" is issue identity + group + root. It's unaffected. The answer row keeps its issue, so it "lands where it would today" (run page lineage, `?issueIdentifier=` reads).
- **Runner, SD (`simple-dispatcher/subscription.js:28-39`, `dispatcher.js:1378`).** `normalizeSubscription` maps any value outside the two-value enum to `null` ("no bubbling edge"). It's read only by the reap liveness gate (`reapers.js` `hasLiveSubscribedChild`). `'none'` → `null` is semantically exactly right, so **no SD change is needed**. Runner kit (`lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`) never reads `subscription`.
- **Docs (`lib/proxy-instructions.js:805, 823, 852, 860-861`).** These describe `subscription` as `"terminal-only|everything"` and as "which of THIS item's events wake the session named in sessionId". They must gain `'none'` (follow-up only) and state that kickoff refuses it.
- **Pinned vocabulary tests.** `tests/unit/dispatch-fields.test.js`, `proxy-dispatch-subscribe.test.js`, `proxy-recommend-dispatch-subscribe.test.js`, `proxy-autopilot-variant.test.js` and `lin-3487-entrance-messages.test.js` pin the "subscription must be one of" text or enum. They will need updating with the new value and message.
- **Liveness alarms (`lib/liveness-detectors.js:470-478`).** These are advisory only. A follow-up row dispatched after a `[pending]` counts as "answered", and that's unchanged. A suppressed wake never creates a lost-wake alarm, because the alarm is about a *parked parent waiting on a dead child*. One edge case to record: if an autopilot is *still running and parked* on the worker when a person sends a `'none'` question to that worker, the answer won't wake it. That's the requested behaviour.
- **Wake shadow (`lib/wake-shadow.js`).** It classifies minted wakes only. If nothing is minted, nothing is recorded.
- **CI-wake sweep (`lib/ci-wake-sweep.js`).** This is a sweep-time producer for PENDING-external parked lineages, not finish-time. It skips autopilot/wake lineages (LIN-3904). A question follow-up that ends `[done]` isn't parked. No interaction.
- **Past behaviour.** Every existing follow-up (no `subscription`, or `'terminal-only'`/`'everything'`) must wake exactly as today, including the stepper beats (`lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js:99-176` sends `subscription:'everything'` on beats, and those wakes actually come from the root edge). The spike's second case confirms that a *real* follow-up chained **after** a `'none'` question still wakes, because the gate keys on the producing row only.

### Options considered
- **A. `subscription: 'none'` on a follow-up (recommended).** It reuses the existing field whose documented meaning is "which of this item's events wake the session". Storage, archive and formatters already carry it, and SD already reads unknown values as "no edge". It's declared, not inferred (§6). It must be refused without `followUpTo`: a fresh worker with `'none'` would leave its orchestrator hanging, which would break the §5 "terminals always bubble on an edge" guarantee. The tax is that the enum now has a value that's legal on follow-ups only. That's one cross-field rule, in the same style as `force`/`cascade`.
- **B. A new boolean (`wake:false` / `quiet:true` / `noWake`).** This would add a second representation of "does this item's finish wake the parent" next to `subscription`. It would need new every-hop plumbing (the LIN-1698/1751 silent-drop class) and SD intake. Rejected.
- **C. `kind: 'question'`.** `kind` is the prompt-template classification and drives churn/cost/session-id rules (LIN-4025). Overloading it with wake semantics mixes two axes. Rejected.
- **D. Infer "question" from the prompt or from ticket state (e.g. ticket Done).** This violates "declared on the edge, never inferred" (`lib/dispatch-wake.js:49-54`). Ticket state is also the wrong signal: real rework on a Done ticket must still wake. Rejected.
- **E. Gate on the autopilot being finished.** That's a LIN-4080-style parent check. But a finished autopilot is exactly what a *real* follow-up needs to wake. Rejected.

### Spike of option A
I patched `addFeedback` with `if (newWake && doc.followUpTo && doc.subscription === 'none') nullWakeReason = 'unsubscribed-follow-up'; else if (newWake) { …existing… }`. Results:
- The question follow-up mints 0 wakes, and its `[done] answered` lands on its own row.
- A real follow-up chained on the question mints the wake.
- The existing suites `dispatch-wake*`, `lin-4080-run-stopped-wake-gate`, `dispatch-store-followup` and `lin-3134-wake-declared` pass: 136/136.

The patch was reverted, so the tree is clean.

### Decisions recorded (engineering, mine to make)
- Suppress **every** wake event from a `'none'` follow-up (`[done]`/`[failed]`/`[blocked]`/`[pending]`). "Doesn't wake anything when it finishes" plus `[blocked]` already reaching the human through rulings means the autopilot has nothing to do with it.
- The gate keys on the **producing row** (`doc`), not on the resolved edge. So only that question is silent, and later rows on the same lineage behave as today.
- Refuse `'none'` without `followUpTo` (400, the shared entrance step). This refuses it on kickoff automatically.

### Close the set
The searches that bound the layers:
- `grep SUBSCRIPTION_LEVELS|isValidSubscription|DEFAULT_SUBSCRIPTION` → `dispatch-fields.js`, `dispatch-entrance.js`, `routes/proxy.js` (an unused import at `:42`).
- `grep -E '\.subscription\b|subscription ===|subscription:'` over lib/routes/public → only `dispatch-fields`, `dispatch-wake`, `dispatch-entrance` and the kickoff prompt.
- The `addItem` census → 4 callers.
- `grep followUpTo` across routes → the producer list below.
- `subscription` in simple-dispatcher → `subscription.js`, `dispatcher.js`, `reapers.js`.

For this set to be wrong, a wake would have to be minted outside `addFeedback`, or a reader of `subscription` would have to exist outside these files. The census test and the greps came back empty for both.

**Surface Assessment: [lands cleanly]**. This extends the existing `subscription` model (one enum value, one cross-field rule, one gate at the existing seam). It adds no second representation and needs no SD/runner change. An improvement I noticed but didn't require: the unused `isValidSubscription/DEFAULT_SUBSCRIPTION/SUBSCRIPTION_LEVELS` import at `routes/proxy.js:42` can be dropped inline.

### Plan Review Verdict
**Verdict:** Approve. The cause is right, the gate is in the right place and keyed on the right row, and the plan covers what was asked. The notes below are corrections the builder can make without changing the plan's design.

**What I checked (LinearViewer `ff1f4aa5` = origin/main; the one commit since the ticket was created touches only task-page files):**
- **Cause.** `addFeedback` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:3286-3336`) calls `_resolveEdgeDoc` (`:2971`), which always walks `followUpTo` up to the chain root. `buildWakeFollowUp` (`lib/dispatch-wake.js:166-229`) has no follow-up guard and builds the wake from that root, and terminals always bubble. A `none` row always has `followUpTo`, so it can never be the resolved edge. Gating on `doc` therefore silences only that row.
- **Gate placement.** Writing it as `if (newWake && doc.followUpTo && doc.subscription === 'none') … else if (newWake) {…}` leaves `wakeFollowUp` null and `markTerminalOnEdge` false. That skips `_wakeParentStopped`, the grant lookup, provisioning, the `_mintWake` CAS and the `[pending]` `addItem`. The `null-wake` log at `:3489` records the reason. The `[aborted]` queued-wake cleanup (`:3504`) still runs, which is correct.
- **Storage.** `inheritFromAnchor` (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:704`) never touches `subscription`. `ROW_FIELDS.subscription` (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:381`) stores the caller's value. So a `none` row keeps `none`.
- **Vocabulary.** `SUBSCRIPTION_LEVELS` has one owner (`dispatch-wake.js:56`), and its only validator is `RUN_FIELD_RULES.subscription` → the entrance step at `:225`, used by S, P, R and K. No other validator reads it. The only other import is the unused one at `routes/proxy.js:42`.
- **Simple-dispatcher.** `normalizeSubscription('none')` → `null`. The reap gate reads it through `parentSessionId: item.sessionId`, and follow-up rows carry no `sessionId`, so a `none` follow-up changes nothing in SD.
- **Tests.** All six named tests exist. `lin-4080-addItem-census.test.js:29,31` currently say "gated upstream in addFeedback (parent-stopped)" only, so the plan's conditional edit is needed.

**Notes for the builder (none blocking):**

1. **The kickoff "refused with no extra code" premise only holds if the body has no `followUpTo`.** The kickoff step input is `{...body, …}` (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1770`), and the kickoff lane never validates or stores `followUpTo`. So `POST /autopilot/kickoff` with a stray `"followUpTo": "x", "subscription": "none"` passes the new rule. It then stores `subscription: 'none'` on an autopilot row (`:1880`) that has no `followUpTo`. The store gate stays inert, but SD reads `none` as "not a subscribed child". A coordinator's reap gate would then stop protecting a live child autopilot, which is exactly what the guard exists to prevent.
   - **Fix:** set `followUpTo: undefined` in the kickoff lane's step input, since kickoff has no follow-up.
   - **Witness:** add a kickoff case that sends a stray `followUpTo` with `none` and expects 400.
2. **Use the existing presence test for `followUpTo`.** For "has followUpTo", use the same test as `isFreshDispatch` (`:120`, `followUpTo !== undefined && followUpTo !== null`) rather than truthiness, so `none` refusal agrees with `entryRung`/`stopAt`/`variant`. The `subscription` step runs before `payload` in S and P. A malformed `followUpTo` is still refused by `payload`, so nothing gets through, but a malformed id with `none` will get the `payload` message rather than the `none` one.
3. **Describe the edge case as what it really is.** Feedback ownership moves to the follow-up row (SD `signalFollowUp`/`resumeSession` set `itemMetadata.itemId = followUpItem.id`). So a `none` follow-up silences everything that session reports during that turn, not only the answer. A session parked on `[pending]` or held at `AWAITING_FOLLOWUP` that finishes its real work while answering will post that real `[done]` onto the `none` row, and the parent is never woken. That is consistent with the plan's decision ("an autopilot still parked on a worker is not woken"). The docs must say it plainly, though, because autopilots read `proxy-instructions`. Suggested wording: "`none`: follow-up only. Nothing that session reports while answering wakes anyone. Use it only for questions to a session whose work is finished. Never use it on a follow-up to your own workers." Put it in `lib/proxy-instructions.js` next to the "terminal-only|everything" text.
4. **Two more doc places name the subscription vocabulary.** Update both alongside `lib/proxy-instructions.js`:
   - `docs/proxy-integration.md:154`
   - `docs/dispatch-protocol.md:135` (the enum row; the bubbling matrix at `:108` covers edges, so a one-line note that `none` is a follow-up-row value outside the matrix is enough)

   Closing search: `grep -rn "terminal-only" docs lib public` (the `docs/papers` and `docs/reviews` hits are historical and can be skipped).
5. **The store witness should check the edge doc directly.** Assert that the root edge doc's `terminalWakeItems` and `wakeWitnessMeta` are unchanged after a `none` `[done]`. Then post a real `[done]` on a later non-`none` row and assert it wakes. That is the burn-before-decide regression the plan names.

The plan fits one session. It goes to `implementation` with these notes.

Implementation done. PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2258 (branch `feat/lin-4166-none-subscription-question`, commit `7d409a89`).

**What changed:** `subscription: "none"` is now a follow-up-only value. It is refused without `followUpTo` (400 `subscription 'none' requires followUpTo`), including on kickoff with a stray `followUpTo`. A finishing follow-up declared `none` mints no wake for `[done]`/`[failed]`/`[blocked]`/`[pending]`. The gate sits before edge resolution, so no grant or `terminalWakeItems` slot is burned. The answer still lands on the follow-up row, and a real follow-up chained after it still wakes. No simple-dispatcher or runner change. Docs updated in `proxy-instructions`, `proxy-integration` and `dispatch-protocol`.

**Evidence:**
- Full unit suite: 22,596 tests, 0 failures. Hermetic keyed arm: exit 0.
- Mutation check: disabling the store gate turns 6 new tests red, disabling the entrance rule turns 7 red, removing kickoff's `followUpTo` clearing turns 2 red. Files restored and re-run green.
- CI on the PR: `CI success` pass; Unit tests pass (9m13s); E2E shards 1–4 pass; Secret scan pass.

**Not done:** the "question only" toggle on the run-page reply box and Flight Companion (out of scope per the plan). Merge is left to review.

## Review — LIN-4166

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2258 at head `7d409a8979abaa4d6d8ddea1c9d35a6209c9a70c` (branch `feat/lin-4166-none-subscription-question`). origin/main has not moved past the PR's base. The PR is MERGEABLE.

CI: green on `7d409a89`: `CI success`, Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4 and Secret scan all SUCCESS (completed 18:19:50Z).

### Scope vs plan
The change touches the places the plan named: the enum (`lib/dispatch-wake.js`), the entrance rule (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js`), the store gate (`lib/dispatch-store.js` addFeedback), the docs (`lib/proxy-instructions.js`, plus `docs/proxy-integration.md` and `docs/dispatch-protocol.md` from plan-review note 4), and the census and vocabulary tests. It adds no other files and does not overrun the plan. All five plan-review notes are handled:
1. Kickoff clears `followUpTo` in its step input.
2. The `followUpTo` presence test is `!== undefined && !== null`, not truthiness.
3. The docs use the suggested "never on your own workers" wording.
4. Both extra docs are updated.
5. The store witness checks the edge doc's `terminalWakeItems` and `wakeWitnessMeta` directly.

`proxy-recommend-dispatch-subscribe` and `proxy-autopilot-variant` needed no edit: neither pins the enum list or `'none'`.

### What I checked
- **Gate placement and keying.** `unsubscribedFollowUp` is decided before `_resolveEdgeDoc`, so `wakeFollowUp` stays null. `_wakeParentStopped`, the grant lookup, provisioning, the `_mintWake` CAS and the `[pending]` addItem are all skipped. `nullWakeReason = 'unsubscribed-follow-up'` reaches the null-wake log. The gate keys on `doc`. A `none` row always has `followUpTo`, so it is never the resolved edge.
- **Entrance.** Every lane with a `subscription` step sends `followUpTo` in its step input: session and proxy use the body, recommend uses `{...body}` (`dispatch-entrance.js:1473`), and kickoff forces `undefined` (`:1786`).
- **Simple-dispatcher (`6060e4f`).** `normalizeSubscription('none')` returns `null`. Both follow-up repoints (`dispatcher.js:332`, `:390`) spread the existing `itemMetadata` and never overwrite `subscription` from the follow-up item. So a `none` follow-up cannot strip a worker session's own subscribed edge or weaken the reap gate. No SD change is needed, as the plan said.
- **Regression check.** `git log` over the touched lib files shows nothing since the ticket was created. LIN-4080's stopped-run gate is intact: the new branch is an `if`/`else if` placed in front of it, and the stopped-run code is unchanged. The census POSITIONS comment is updated.
- **Doc sweep.** `grep -rln terminal-only docs lib public`: the remaining hits (`llms.txt`, `observation-sessions-materializer.js`) use "terminal-only" in an unrelated sense.
- **Targeted suites on the head.** 10 files (the new test, the subscribe, recommend, autopilot-variant, entrance-message, dispatch-fields and census tests, `lin-4080-run-stopped-wake-gate`, `dispatch-store-followup`, `lin-3134-wake-declared`): 161/161 pass.
- **Mutation checks.** Each mutation was reverted afterwards and the tree is clean.
  - Store gate disabled (`=== 'NEVER'`): 6 red. That is every addFeedback case, including the "real follow-up after a question" count.
  - Entrance `none` rule disabled: 4 red (proxy fresh, session fresh, session null-`followUpTo`, kickoff).
  - Kickoff `followUpTo: undefined` removed: 1 red (kickoff with a stray `followUpTo`).
  - Presence test narrowed to `=== undefined`: 1 red (the null-`followUpTo` case).
- **Isolated, or one of a class?** It is one gate at the single wake seam, and the census bounds the producers to 4. Follow-up producers that hard-code their fields (Flight Companion, proposal Apply) send no `subscription` and keep waking, as the plan intends. The CI-wake sweep and wake mints never send `none`. No unhandled sibling is inside scope.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (class: follow-up producers that accept `subscription`; plan Witness 3). The recommend-and-dispatch lane's handling of `none` is not pinned by any test. I ran it in a scratch test, since deleted:
  - `none` without `followUpTo` gives the expected 400 `subscription 'none' requires followUpTo` and enqueues nothing.
  - `none` with `followUpTo` gets past the entrance rule. In that harness it then 500s on the anchor's Linear lookup, and so does every other subscription value.

  **Before the merge**, close-out adds the refusal case to `tests/unit/proxy-recommend-dispatch-subscribe.test.js`: POST `/api/proxy/recommend-and-dispatch` `{issueIdentifier:'TEST-1', kind:'implementation', subscription:'none'}` → 400 with that exact message and `captured.item === undefined`. Tell right from wrong by this check: the test goes red when the `none` line in `subscriptionFailure` is disabled.
- **Inside** (the plan's Done-when on the live path). A real runner session answering a `none` follow-up posts its `[done]` on the follow-up row and mints no `kind:'wake'` row. The store tests drive this with mock collections; no automated test runs it end to end through the runner. **After the deploy:** send `POST /api/proxy/dispatch {followUpTo:<finished session's row>, subscription:'none', prompt:'…'}` on a ticket whose autopilot is finished. Check that the answer lands on that row and that no wake row with `followUpTo:<autopilot id>` appears (`GET /dispatch?issueIdentifier=…`). The server log should show a null-wake entry with reason `unsubscribed-follow-up`.
- **Rollback:** revert the PR's merge commit. This is reversible. Rows already stored with `subscription:'none'` keep the value through `dispatch-fields`, so after a revert they would simply wake as they did before. No migration is involved.

Fix for close-out to make, a one-line doc correction: `lib/proxy-instructions.js:823` ends "Same contract as on POST /autopilot/kickoff below." That is no longer exact. Change it to: "Same contract as on POST /autopilot/kickoff below, except \"none\", which kickoff refuses."

Outside, for close-out to file if it does not already exist (the plan's decision 6): a "question only" toggle on the run-page reply box and in Flight Companion `send_follow_up`.

Design note, no action: a `none` follow-up to a worker its autopilot is still parked on silences that worker's real terminal during that turn. The plan accepted this, and the docs now say so plainly.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The implementation matches the plan and every plan-review note. The gate is placed and keyed correctly, the load-bearing tests fail under mutation, and CI is green. What remains is the recommend-lane refusal test, the one-line doc fix and the post-deploy live check.

## Close-out — LIN-4166

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2258, squash-merged as `7797c306` (pinned with `--match-head-commit 64e922fe`). Deploy "Harbour / production" for `7797c306` reached `success` at 18:48:26Z.

**CI:** exists (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Final state on `64e922fe`: CI success, Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4 and Secret scan all passed, read fresh before the merge. PR was MERGEABLE and origin/main had not moved.

**Changes I made after the approval (commit `64e922fe`):**
1. Added the recommend-and-dispatch refusal test in `tests/unit/proxy-recommend-dispatch-subscribe.test.js` (`none` without `followUpTo` → 400 `subscription 'none' requires followUpTo`, nothing enqueued). Answers review's "What CI Did Not Prove" item 1. Checked: disabling the `none` rule at `lib/dispatch-entrance.js:129` turns exactly this test red (16 pass / 1 fail); restored, 17/17 pass.
2. Corrected `lib/proxy-instructions.js:823` to end "…below, except "none", which kickoff refuses." Answers review's one-line doc fix. `proxy-instructions.test.js` still passes (63/63 across the touched suites).

**Ledger:**
- Inside, recommend-lane handling of `none`: **settled** by change 1 and its mutation check.
- Inside, live path (a real runner session answering a `none` follow-up mints no wake): **not run**. The close-out token has no dispatch grant (`DISPATCH_GRANT_REQUIRED` on `POST /dispatch`, which is checked before validation, so no probe was possible either). Who can run it: the workspace owner or any session with a dispatch grant. Steps: `POST /api/proxy/dispatch {followUpTo:<finished session row>, subscription:'none', prompt:'…'}`; confirm the answer lands on that row, no `kind:'wake'` row with `followUpTo:<autopilot id>` appears in `GET /dispatch?issueIdentifier=…`, and the server log shows a null-wake entry with reason `unsubscribed-follow-up`. The deploy has landed, so this does not hold the close. For the operator's list.
- Rollback: the review named it: revert the PR's merge commit (`7797c306`). Reversible, no migration; stored `none` rows would simply wake as before.
- Outside, "question only" toggle on the run-page reply box and Flight Companion `send_follow_up`: filed as **LIN-4174** (Feature, front:flight-companion, priority Low, related to this ticket). No existing ticket covered it (searched by title terms and file names; LIN-4166 had no relations).
- Design note (no action, per review): a `none` follow-up to a worker its autopilot is still parked on silences that worker's real terminal; the docs say so.

**Description:** archived first (snapshot `2026-11-03T18:25:03Z` verified identical to the pre-prune description), then pruned: research findings and the implementation plan were replaced with a stub pointing at the PR and snapshots. Why / What we want, the `Implementation Plan` heading, `fits one session` and `plan-review due: no` were kept as written.

Also posted the same close-out note, including the not-run check, on the PR.

## Survey spike 1a (implementation)

**1. Why was this difficult?** It wasn't, much. Research and plan review had already found the seam. These are the places it bound:
- **The entrance step's input.** The shared `subscription` step only read `{subscription}`. Session, proxy and recommend spread `...body` into their check input, so `followUpTo` came for free. Kickoff spreads `body` too, so a stray `followUpTo` would have satisfied the new rule. I had to clear it explicitly in `lib/dispatch-entrance.js`.
- **`addFeedback`.** The method is long, with many hoisted locals. Placing the gate before `_resolveEdgeDoc` was one line. Proving it safe took longer: I checked that every later `edgeDoc` use sits behind `wakeFollowUp` or `markTerminalOnEdge`.
- **Tests that pinned the old shape.** Two tests pinned the exact "must be one of" text (`dispatch-fields`, `lin-3487-entrance-messages`). `proxy-dispatch-subscribe` used `'none'` as its example of an *invalid* value.
- **The enum written out in prose.** It appears in about seven places across three docs and three code comments/JSDoc.
- **Tooling friction, my own.** The session-lane stub needed `getGrantDeclaration`. A zsh no-word-split slip blanked my first mutation run.

**2. What I would have done first.** Nothing large. A small tidy would have helped: the "has followUpTo" presence test (`!== undefined && !== null`) is inlined in `isFreshDispatch`, `proxyContextPolicy`, and now `subscriptionFailure` and the store gate. One shared predicate would make that a single decision. That would have saved this ticket perhaps ten minutes and removed one way to drift. Neither that nor the repeated enum prose justified a wider tidy.

**3. What the ticket or plan got wrong.**
- **Kickoff.** The plan said kickoff refuses `none` "automatically, with no extra code". That was wrong because of the stray-`followUpTo` case. Plan review caught it before I started.
- **Which tests would break.** The plan expected `proxy-recommend-dispatch-subscribe` and `proxy-autopilot-variant` to need updates. They didn't. It missed that `proxy-dispatch-subscribe` used `'none'` as its invalid sample.
- **Docs.** The plan named only `proxy-instructions`; review added two more files.
- **The recommend lane.** The plan's witness list included accepting `none` on the recommend lane. I did not witness that lane directly. It shares the same step and spreads `body`, but that is reasoning, not a test.
